body:
okay i tapped "romanticizing a Tuesday" on Mood just to see what it'd do, and the first song it handed me was The Best Day 🥹

then invisible string. then Timeless. then Daylight. then Mary's Song. five songs, not one of them sad — the exact warm-quiet corner of the catalogue i was fishing for.

that's the whole trick of it: Mood isn't a playlist somebody built, it's the feature reading the vibe you give it and pulling the real songs that match. i handed it an ordinary good day and it gave me the five softest ones.

tag the friend who romanticizes a Tuesday with you — then go pick your own mood on longlivets.com and tell us what it gave you 💛

critique.rationale: The 'what it gave me' Mood slot: tapped the approved chip 'romanticizing a Tuesday' and listed the five real returned songs (The Best Day, invisible string, Timeless, Daylight, Mary's Song — all scored eras). Fan-gush lead, tag-a-friend share hook; proves the site's most distinctive feature works.

why: IG sibling of mood:result:romanticizing-a-tuesday (Calendar 2026-10-21 23:00Z Mood beat). Chip label quoted verbatim from mood-starters.ts; results are deterministic — matchMoods on this chip's hand-tuned vector returns The Best Day [fearless], invisible string [folklore], Timeless [speak-now], Daylight [lover], Mary's Song [debut], all scored eras (verified by running the mood engine on the seed-generated song-moods, since the live site can't be reached from this job). Picked a FRESH joyful chip (feral-about-a-bridge was already posted 08-19, and this counters the catalogue's sad skew). Hook: the artifact (what came back), not a date-stamp. Share hook = tag a friend. Link /?mode=mood (never ?mood=).
